body: [{"streamId":"01a0cf9b-2936-76c7-b214-5811b72b51cf","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0cf9b-2936-76c7-b214-5811b72b51cf\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022One GitHub review request produces exactly one live pr-review task across every node of the owner\\u0027s fleet: when two nodes mint for the same pull request, the younger task is abandoned as a duplicate on every node, before or after a claim, so never two live tasks\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022Root cause is written into the fix\\u0027s own commit and the card: two daemons of one owner, both with the project registered and auto pr-review on under the same GitHub login, each mint a pr-review task for the same review request within seconds; each node keeps its own ObservedReviewRequest record (id prefixed with its own node id) and the store-level task query in CreateOneAsync sees the peer\\u0027s task only when replication lands, about two minutes later, after both dispatchers have claimed; the record names the two aggravating facts from the incident (the loser\\u0027s twin queued under a per-project ceiling of 0 on one node and was claimed on the other after replication, and the two nodes ran different auto pr-review modes because the setting is node-scoped)\u0022,\u0022Convergence on replication: when a pr-review task arrives by replication (task_added header originNodeId set) whose external reference already has a live pr-review task in this store, the younger of the two (by UUIDv7 id, deterministic on every node with no coordination) is abandoned as a duplicate before any dispatcher can claim it, with an abandon reason naming the survivor; a run the younger one already owns is killed and retired as superseded, and the same rule applies when the local task is the younger one\u0022,\u0022The dedup query in CreateOneAsync and the already-covered fast path in DecideAsync treat a replicated live task exactly as a local one, so a node whose sweep runs after the peer\\u0027s task has landed mints nothing and records the peer\\u0027s task as the covering one\u0022,\u0022Tests: a two-store test where both stores mint for the same review request and replication is replayed between them ends with exactly one live task on both sides and the same survivor on both; a replicated younger duplicate arriving after the local one is already claimed is abandoned and its run retired; the mirror case where the local task is the younger one abandons the local task; the existing already-covered fast path test still passes\u0022,\u0022h9k status and the courier feed show the abandoned duplicate once, as a duplicate of the survivor, never as a needs-you row\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Evidence, from both nodes (2026-09-24). Three occurrences on arx-platform: #2140 (2026-09-23): 0222aa22 minted on Windows 18:42:08Z (log: is created), 0ac2114a task_added with originNodeId 01a00d41 (Mac), born 18:42:40Z by UUIDv7, received on Windows 18:44:39Z, claimed there 18:45:22Z. #2143 (2026-09-24): 9233aaaa minted on Windows 15:36:10Z, a3ab84ac from the Mac born 15:36:41Z, received 15:38:04Z, claimed on Windows 15:38:29Z. #2147 (2026-09-24): 5859bfc5 minted on Windows 22:50:17Z, 84e20e28 from the Mac born 22:50:24Z, received 22:52:09Z, claimed on Windows 22:52:32Z, abandoned by hand 22:55:17Z. The Mac\\u0027s h9kd.log has \\u0027is created and reviewing\\u0027 for exactly those three Mac-born ids, each followed minutes later by \\u0027already covers it\\u0027 naming the Windows twin; each node\\u0027s log names only its own mint as created because the dedup query orders by AddedAt over two records. Two facts that shaped the incident: the Mac\\u0027s arx-platform per-project ceiling was 0, so the Mac-born twin queued there and was claimed on Windows after replication (every duplicate run was a Windows run); and the two nodes ran different modes (Mac normal by default, Windows first explicit), because ProjectSettingsChanged is EventScope.NodeScoped and never replicates. mt_doc_observedreviewrequest ids are prefixed with the observing node id by design (Decisions Log #161), so no node reads another\\u0027s record; do not try to share them. Code: src/Hall9k.Daemon/AutoPrReview/AutoPrReviewEngine.cs (DecideAsync near line 439 with the guessed-reference fast path, CreateOneAsync near line 688 with the canonical existing and previousReview queries), src/Hall9k.Connectors/Replication/EventReplicationInbox.cs (applies task_added with originNodeId headers), the DispatchEngine claim path, h9k run kill for retiring a run. Both tasks in each pair were assigned to Brian Hall with no placement, so either dispatcher claims. This task is the convergence layer only: the younger task loses, deterministically, wherever the collision is seen. The hold-before-mint layer (wait one replication interval before a first mint) is a separate task stacked on this one; do not implement it here. Related lesson: dispatched sessions must not run board-mutating h9k commands; the abandon here belongs to the platform, not a session. Since 2026-09-24 20:23 EDT the Mac has arx-platform auto pr-review off, so the live race is closed for that project by configuration; the fix is for any project two nodes both watch. No em dashes in anything authored.\u0022},\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Type\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Model\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022RevisedAt\u0022:\u00222026-09-25T00:31:41.755983\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022RevisedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022EpicId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022QueuePriority\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022ClearInteractiveMode\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022CloseLinkedIssue\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022Constraints\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false}}","originEventId":"a86c950c-09f8-42e2-a015-62d0a08a2b81","originSequence":63895,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-09-25T00:31:41.767556+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a0d5f9-a4f8-7164-9dbc-df8c1cccd3f7","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0d5f9-a4f8-7164-9dbc-df8c1cccd3f7\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022A node that first sees a review request no task covers waits one replication interval before minting, so two nodes that watch the same project mint once between them in the common case instead of converging after a wasted run\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022Hold before mint: a node that observes a review request no live task covers yet does not mint on the sweep that first sees it; it records the observation with the time it was first seen and mints on a later sweep only if, one replication interval later, still nothing covers the reference; a request already held past that window mints at once on the next sweep\u0022,\u0022The interval is a node setting (h9k config set, printed by h9k config show and h9k daemon status with its origin the way default-model is, bound at daemon start like the other DaemonOptions values) whose default is near the message sweep\\u0027s active cadence, and it is zero, so the first sweep mints, when the owner has exactly one enrolled node; an explicit zero on a fleet also mints on the first sweep\u0022,\u0022While a request is held, h9k status shows it as an informational row naming the hold and when it ends, never as a needs-you row, and the daemon log writes one line when the hold starts and one when it ends in a mint or in a peer\\u0027s task covering it, never one per tick\u0022,\u0022Tests: a single-node owner mints on the first sweep with no added latency; a two-store test where both stores observe the same review request within the window and replication is replayed between them ends with exactly one mint and one live task on both sides; a request held past the window mints at once on the next sweep; a request a peer\\u0027s task covers before the window ends mints nothing and records the peer\\u0027s task as covering\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Stacked on b72b51cf (the convergence layer: the younger of two colliding pr-review tasks is abandoned wherever the collision is seen). This task adds the hold in front of the first mint so the common case never collides at all. Brian accepted the price on 2026-09-24: about one replication interval (near two minutes at the message sweep\\u0027s active cadence) between a review request and the review starting on a fleet of two or more nodes; a single-node owner pays nothing. Code: src/Hall9k.Daemon/AutoPrReview/AutoPrReviewEngine.cs (DecideAsync near line 439, CreateOneAsync near line 688, the ObservedReviewRequest record written per sweep with its outcome), src/Hall9k.Daemon/DaemonOptions.cs (the message sweep cadence floor near line 132 is the natural default), h9k config set and the OperatingSettings report for the new node setting, following the DefaultModel pattern (Decisions Log #33) and the effort knob just shipped in #584. How the daemon knows the owner has exactly one node is for the build to settle from the owner\\u0027s own enrolled, unrevoked node set (h9k node, idea 202383dc T1) rather than from replication peers seen so far; the challenge session will check that seam. The ObservedReviewRequest record already exists per sweep and per node; the hold should ride on it (first-seen time and a Held outcome) rather than a new document. Do not change the convergence layer here.
